summary: Sir Trevor Mallard, born in 1954, is a New Zealand politician and diplomat. A Labour MP from 1984 to 1990 and from 1993 to 2022, he served as Speaker of the House of Representatives from 2017 to 2022. In the Fifth Labour Government, from 1999 to 2008, he was a Cabinet minister, mainly for education and state services. Teachers' unions strongly criticised his time as education minister, over pay disputes and school closures. He had a reputation as a political fighter and was convicted of fighting in a public place after punching National MP Tau Henare in 2007. As Speaker he made Parliament more family-friendly and dropped the rule that male MPs wear ties, though some of his actions during the 2022 Wellington protests drew criticism. He was New Zealand's ambassador to Ireland from 2023 until Foreign Minister Winston Peters recalled him in August 2025.
